errors: Says a bookmarked link will work, but the chosen auth is an Authorization: Bearer header, which a browser link cannot send.
Defaults to since/until filters and sorting on updated_at while itself noting that bulkImport leaves updated_at stale.
Formula guard is applied to the numeric total too, so a negative total would be exported as text with a leading apostrophe.
Includes customer e-mail by default without treating it as data to minimise.
H1-A.note: Well grounded and covers nearly every trap with streaming, LEFT JOIN and a rollout note about breaking the import caller, but five questions, a README typo fix, no open-the-real-file check and no rollback statement.

errors: Accepts the token as a ?token= query parameter, which leaks into logs and browser history (acknowledged in the response).
SQL uses SELECT o.* although the output is allow-listed through COLUMNS.
H1-B.note: Three sharp questions with defaults, a fail-closed token that still works from a bookmark, a full HTTP-level test with awkward data and a real-file check; never says outright that no admin UI exists, omits that items and addresses are absent, and gives no rollback statement.

errors: Ships the endpoint unauthenticated by default (flagged, and customer data is deliberately excluded).
No UTF-8 BOM, and the whole list is built with .all() in memory (acknowledged).
H1-C.note: Lean and accurate about the repo (no UI, no auth, no items or addresses, unreliable updated_at, no created_at) and keeps PII out, but leaves the route open, has only a service-level test, no real-file check and no rollback statement.

errors: The delivered default (Bearer header) cannot be used from a browser download; the response admits this and defers the fix to a follow-up.
The auth check is only verified manually, not in the test file.
H1-D.note: Sound CSV and token gating with no PII, but it never states that no admin UI exists, does not mention the missing items and addresses, lists the updated_at gap without its effect on the export, and leaves staff without a workable way to download.

errors: Exports raw total_cents with no decision on money format.
Non sequitur: e-mail is left out 'because the schema has no address to ship to'.
Suggests a date filter as the scaling fix although the only date column is unreliable and that is not discussed.
The 'Failure modes covered' checklist includes items that do not apply.
H1-E.note: Basic auth is the right fit for a browser download and the HTTP test is real, but there is no filter, the whole table is loaded with .all(), cents are exported raw and the updated_at problem is listed without its consequence.

errors: An X-Admin-Token header cannot be sent from a browser download; acknowledged but left unresolved ('the admin page (if one exists)').
The test inserts an order with user_id 99 and no such user; better-sqlite3 enables foreign keys by default as far as I recall, so this insert would likely fail (not run here).
Auth lives inside the route handler and has no automated test.
H1-F.note: Good CSV, streaming, LEFT JOIN and PII minimisation, but it never establishes that no admin UI exists, omits the missing items and addresses, pads with a failure checklist and leaves the download unusable from a browser.

errors: The test file is described with one example rather than written out.
Five questions, two of which overlap (how staff log in, whether to protect the import route).
H1-G.note: Best read of the repo (no UI, no auth, no created_at, no addresses, tracking codes as untrusted input) with browser-friendly fail-closed Basic auth, streaming and integer money maths; it fixes the README typo unasked and gives no rollback statement.

errors: Ships customer names on an unauthenticated endpoint by default, relying on an unverified assumption that the service is internal-only.
The whole export is built with .all() in memory (acknowledged).
H1-H.note: Very well grounded, including the warning not to re-upload the file to the shipment import, with an HTTP-level test, but it follows the open-route pattern while exporting names, does not stream, and has no real-file check or rollback statement.
